topic: Delivery times of three couriers for refrigerated medicine
decision: which courier to contract for refrigerated medicine deliveries next year

columns.ship_date: date the parcel left the pharmacy
columns.promised_hours: delivery time promised to the customer, hours
columns.cost_usd: price paid to the courier, US dollars
columns.customer_rating: customer rating of the delivery, 1 to 5

findings.text: Courier prices are within 50 cents of each other ($9.28 to $9.73 per delivery).
Customer ratings are similar (4.2 to 4.3 out of 5).
Cold packs keep these medicines safe for 48 hours. Swiftline delivered 14.4% of parcels after more than 48 hours, against 2.2% for Northway and 2.5% for ParcelPro.
Rural deliveries take about 4 hours longer than urban and suburban ones.
Swiftline is fastest on a typical delivery: a median of 17.9 hours, against 22.5 for Northway and 21.2 for ParcelPro.
Parcels shipped on Mondays take longest, because of the weekend backlog.
Overall, 17% of deliveries arrived after the time promised to the customer.
ParcelPro only started in September, so its figures rest on 40 deliveries, against 90 for each of the others. Its single delivery over 48 hours could easily be two or three in a larger sample.
Delivery time rises with distance (correlation 0.39 for deliveries under 48 hours).

main.gist: Swiftline is fast on a typical day but too often breaks the 48-hour limit

caveat.gist: ParcelPro's numbers rest on only 40 deliveries
